answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so each node’s influence decays with distance and is constrained by transition mixing. A Sybil cluster typically attaches through a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits escape probability, while min-cut transitivity bounds its stationary mass and aggregate voting weight. Thus pigment, velvet, and jetty identities cannot amplify support without trusted cross-cut attestations.
